page: Vultr vbm-8c-64gb-amd is a bare-metal server belonging to the Bare Metal NVMe family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 4345P processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, featuring 8 physical cores and 16 virtual CPUs with dedicated allocation. The processor operates at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz and is equipped with 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. The server is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided by a 3890 GB local NVMe SSD, and the system includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, scoring in the top 10% for stress-ng single-core CPU tests, Geekbench single-core metrics, and single-threaded operations such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. Multi-core performance is strong, with the Geekbench multi-core score placing in the top 25%, while stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores fall within the average range. Memory performance is mixed; the PassMark memory score ranks in the top 10%, and read-only memory bandwidth is average, but large-block write memory bandwidth is positioned in the bottom 25%. For specialized tasks, the server achieves top-tier results in image and text processing, alongside strong prompt processing and top-tier text generation speeds for small language models.

The hardware profile offers high resource density, combining dedicated bare-metal CPU execution with a substantial 3890 GB NVMe storage capacity, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring direct hardware access without virtualization overhead. However, the write memory bandwidth for large blocks represents a performance tradeoff. This server is suited for database hosting, local storage-heavy applications, static web serving, text and image processing pipelines, and lightweight language model inference.
